paragraphs.source_en: 1 (p. 34) “her husband was her cousin also”: Marriage between cousins was acceptable throughout much of the nineteenth century, when such arrangements consolidated family property. Realistic in this regard, the quasi-incestuous relationships represented in Wuthering Heights are also typical of Gothic literature.

paragraphs.source_en: 3 (p. 36) she commenced: The device of having a faithful retainer narrate a family saga is also present in Maria Edgeworth’s Castle Rackrent (1800), in which the devoted Thady Quirk tells the story of three generations of the Rackrents, a family of Irish landowners. Both a historical and a regional novel, Castle Rackrent was an important precedent for the work of Sir Walter Scott. See above, chapter 1, note 1.

paragraphs.source_en: 4 (p. 37) Liverpool: Liverpool, situated where the River Mersey meets the Irish Sea, became a major center for the British slave trade in the eighteenth century. The port was extensively populated by transient foreigners and was also a refuge for the Irish, who fled famines in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
